label: Hooks are declared in .vibe/hooks.toml or ~/.vibe/hooks.toml as [[hooks]] entries with name, type, command, match, timeout (60s default), strict and description, stable with no opt-in flag.

Seven hook events exist (post_agent, pre_tool, post_tool, pre_agent, notification, session_start, session_end); only pre_tool, post_tool and pre_agent accept strict, which is where a failing hook may block.
Hook provenance spans host, project, project-plugin, global, global-plugin and client sources, and HookProtocol accepts VIBE, CLAUDE_CODE and KIMI_CODE.
A resolved hook carries cwd, environment, order, visibility, protocol, plugin name and config file, enough to run a repository guard from its own checkout.

Approval modes are agent safety levels SAFE, NEUTRAL, DESTRUCTIVE, SMART and YOLO, with builtin ask, accept-edits, smart-approve, auto-approve, explore and lean agents, and per-tool ALWAYS, NEVER or ASK permission.
The workspace boundary is a policy: outside_workdir is ask (default) or deny, overridable per tool, enable_auto_approve can forbid YOLO, and project config plus AGENTS.md are gated by folder trust.
Writes that would decide what executes next (.vibe config, .git/hooks, .git/config, shell startup files) escalate to a human; the module states it is a heuristic, not a boundary.
There is no user-facing sandbox mode in 3.1.2: no schema field and no CLI flag, while the harness ships a Sandbox Environment adapter, so sandboxing is a deployment choice.
The eight enforcement guards port to pre_tool or post_tool strict hooks with a payload adapter and a state directory; the OpenCode tool.execute payload shape does not carry over.
Turn-stopping guards cannot block on Vibe: completion-evidence and ask-surface-guard map to post_agent, which has no strict mode, and the goal/session adapters have no Vibe event.
